lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: Life Cycles and Reproduction
lesson.summary: Life cycles of mammals, birds, amphibians and insects compared.
learning_objectives: Describe the life cycle of a mammal, bird, amphibian and insect
Compare how they are alike and different
Explain why habitats matter for young animals

standards.text: Describe the life process of reproduction in some plants and animals; describe the life cycle of a mammal, an amphibian, an insect and a bird

success_criteria: I can order the stages in a life cycle
I can say how a frog and a butterfly change
I can say how to protect young animals
lesson.real_life: Watching frogspawn in spring, butterflies in the garden and chicks hatching on a farm.

warm_up.prompt: All living things grow and change.

blocks.say: Welcome, young scientist! Today we follow the growing-up stories of mammals, birds, frogs and insects.

blocks.alt: A lamb, a hen, a frog and a butterfly.
blocks.caption: A lamb, a hen, a frog and a butterfly.

blocks.markdown: A **mammal** has fur or hair and feeds its young milk.
blocks.say: Mammals have hair or fur. Their babies are born alive, and they drink their mother's milk. Humans are mammals, and mammals are animals.

blocks.alt: A white lamb standing in a green field beside two sheep
blocks.caption: A lamb is a young mammal.
blocks.credit: Photo by Matt Seymour on Unsplash
blocks.say: This lamb is a young mammal. A mammal's life cycle is baby, young animal, then adult. The adult can have babies of its own.

question.prompt: How does a baby mammal get its first food?
question.explanation: Baby mammals drink their mother's milk.

blocks.markdown: A **bird** lays eggs and sits on them to keep them warm.
blocks.say: Birds lay eggs. A hen sits on her eggs to keep them warm. Inside, the chick grows for about three weeks, then hatches.

scenes.caption: Egg in the nest.
scenes.say: A hen lays an egg. She keeps it warm in a nest.

scenes.caption: Chick to adult.
scenes.say: After about three weeks, the chick hatches. It grows into a hen that can lay eggs of her own.

question.prompt: A hen's egg hatches after a few minutes.
question.hint: The chick needs time to grow.
question.explanation: A chick needs about three weeks to grow before it hatches.

blocks.title: Four growing-up stories
blocks.transcript: First, a butterfly. It starts as a tiny egg on a leaf. A caterpillar hatches and eats leaves. Then it makes a pupa, and changes inside. An adult butterfly comes out. It is the same animal, but changed. Next, a frog. Frogspawn in the pond hatches into tadpoles. The tadpole grows legs and lungs. It becomes a froglet, then a frog. A hen lays an egg and sits on it. After three weeks, a chick hatches. A lamb is born alive. It drinks milk and grows into a sheep. Safe habitats help all young animals grow. We can help them too!
blocks.caption: A butterfly, a frog, a hen and a lamb each tell their story.

points: Mammals are born alive and drink milk
blocks.say: Remember. Mammals are born alive and drink milk. Birds lay eggs. Both grow up and have young.

An animal with fur or hair that feeds its young milk.
An animal with feathers that lays eggs.

The young of an animal.

mini_quiz.explanation: A hen is a bird and lays eggs.

mini_quiz.prompt: Match each animal to its young.
mini_quiz.explanation: A sheep has a lamb, a hen has a chick, a dog has a puppy.

mini_quiz.prompt: The time a mammal baby grows inside its mother is called...
mini_quiz.explanation: Gestation is the time before birth.

blocks.markdown: **Frogspawn** is a mass of jelly eggs laid in water.
blocks.say: Frogs are amphibians. A frog starts as frogspawn, a mass of jelly eggs laid in water. Frogs lay lots of eggs in spring.

blocks.alt: Green frogs sitting on a rock in a pond
blocks.caption: Adult frogs by a pond.
blocks.credit: Photo by Denley Photography on Unsplash
blocks.say: These adult frogs live near the pond. After the monsoon rains, frogs gather to breed. A tadpole hatches with gills and a tail. It slowly grows legs and lungs.

scenes.caption: Tadpole: gills and tail.
scenes.say: Frogspawn hatches into tadpoles. A tadpole has a tail and gills, and it lives in water.

scenes.caption: Froglet to frog.
scenes.say: Legs grow, the tail shrinks, and lungs develop. A froglet can leave the water, and becomes an adult frog.

question.prompt: What does a tadpole breathe with?
question.explanation: A tadpole breathes with gills. An adult frog uses lungs.

blocks.markdown: **Metamorphosis** is a big change in body shape as an animal grows.
blocks.say: A tadpole's change into a frog is called metamorphosis. It is the same animal, with a very different body.

blocks.title: Order the frog
blocks.goal: Move the pictures to the right pond.

blocks.title: Pond watch
materials: A pond, if a grown-up can take you
instructions: Look for frogspawn in spring. Count the groups.
Look again each week for tadpoles.
Return and observe. Never take frogspawn home.

question.prompt: A tadpole and a frog are two different animals.
question.explanation: They are the same animal at different stages.

points: A tadpole grows legs and lungs
Metamorphosis is a big change in body shape
blocks.say: Remember. Frogspawn, tadpole, froglet, then adult frog. The changes are called metamorphosis.

terms.meaning: Animals like frogs that live in water and on land.
A mass of jelly eggs.
A big change in body shape.

Parts that let animals breathe underwater.

mini_quiz.explanation: Frogspawn, tadpole, froglet, then adult frog.
A froglet has legs and a shrinking tail.
Adult frogs use lungs, and their skin too.

blocks.markdown: A **larva** hatches from an egg. A caterpillar is a butterfly's larva.
blocks.say: A butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf. A larva, called a caterpillar, hatches. Its job is to eat and grow.

blocks.alt: An orange and black butterfly resting on green leaves
blocks.caption: An adult butterfly.
blocks.credit: Photo by Natalie Wagner on Unsplash
blocks.say: The caterpillar changes into a pupa. Inside, it is alive and changing. Then an adult butterfly comes out, like this one resting on a leaf. Butterflies fly in the Margalla Hills.

scenes.caption: Egg and larva.
scenes.say: Egg, then larva. The caterpillar eats leaves and grows.

scenes.caption: Pupa to adult.
scenes.say: The pupa is not moving, but it is alive. Inside, the body is changing. An adult butterfly emerges.

question.prompt: What is the stage after the larva?
question.explanation: A butterfly goes egg, larva, pupa, adult.

blocks.markdown: A frog has gills, then lungs. A butterfly has a pupa stage.
blocks.say: A frog and a butterfly both change a lot. A frog has four stages. A butterfly has four stages too, but they are different.

blocks.alt: Frog and butterfly: two kinds of metamorphosis.
blocks.caption: Frog and butterfly: two kinds of metamorphosis.

blocks.title: Life cycle match
blocks.say: Flip the cards and find the matching pairs. A little brain break!

question.prompt: The animal in a pupa is dead because it does not move.
question.explanation: The insect is alive and changing inside the pupa.

points: Insects go through egg, larva, pupa, adult
The pupa is alive and changing
A butterfly's story differs from a frog's
blocks.say: Remember. Insects have egg, larva, pupa and adult stages. The pupa is alive.

terms.meaning: The young stage of an insect that hatches from an egg.
The stage where an insect changes inside a case.

blocks.markdown: A **habitat** is where an animal lives.
blocks.say: A habitat is the place where an animal lives. Young animals need a safe habitat with food, water and shelter.

blocks.alt: Trees, ponds and nests are habitats.
blocks.caption: Trees, ponds and nests are habitats.

blocks.say: Some habitats are in danger. If a habitat is lost, animals may become endangered. In Pakistan, the markhor and the snow leopard are endangered.

question.prompt: Why do young animals need a safe habitat?
question.explanation: A habitat gives food, water and shelter.

options.text: To find food, water and shelter

blocks.say: Adaptation takes many, many generations. Animals cannot change quickly when a habitat disappears.

blocks.title: Wildlife helper plan
instructions: Draw a plan for a small wildlife corner at school.
Add a bowl of water and some wildflowers.
Add a nest box or a bug hotel.
Tell your class about your plan.
blocks.say: Children can help. Keep ponds clean, put up a nest box, plant flowers for insects, and do not disturb nests. Never take frogspawn home.

blocks.alt: A nest box, wildflowers and a clean pond help wildlife.
blocks.caption: A nest box, wildflowers and a clean pond help wildlife.

blocks.prompt: What could happen to tadpoles if a pond is polluted? Have a think first.
blocks.answer_markdown: Many would die. They live in the water, so polluted water harms their gills.

question.prompt: Children can help protect young animals.
question.explanation: Children can plant flowers, keep ponds clean and build nest boxes.

points: Habitats in danger lead to endangered animals
blocks.say: Remember. Safe habitats help young animals grow. Everyone can help protect them.
